issue_context.title: drivers: dma: dma_mcux_lpc: uses wrong transfer size for I2S
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
In a change that went in between v3.3 and v3.4, the dma_mcux_lpc driver was changed to support transfers larger than one descriptor allowed for (which is 1024 words).

That change introduced a regression which causes I2S to not work on chips like RT595.

The regression is due to how the DMA transfer size is computed. The old version used the dest_data_size for transfer size (which really isn't correct either, like if it was doing an I2S RX ) but the latest version uses MIN(dest_data_size, source_data_size). The I2S driver (i2s_mcux_flexcomm), when doing TX, always sets source_data_size to 1, but dest_data_size to 1 or 4, depending on the bits in the I2S config, with 4 being typical for 16-bit PCM two channel. The result of the bug is that the DMA transfers 1 byte to the I2S FIFO, when it is expecting 4.

**To Reproduce**

I had expected the i2s_speed test under tests/drivers/i2s to catch this, but it did not. My only guess as to why is because the bug impacts both the I2S TX and RX the same way, so the RX would up getting what it expected, even though it was actually being clocked out incorrectly.

The RT595EVK config configures flexcomm3 for TX and flexcomm1 for RX, but makes them actually share  DATA, WS, and CLK.

To reproduce the problem, I created a config such that flexcomm1 was TX, flexcomm3 was unused, and I was transmitting I2S intended for the TFA9896 amp on the board. Putting the I2S output on an analyzer, it was clear that the data was incorrect when writing to the I2S one byte at a time when it was expected 4 (two channels of 16-bits each).

**Expected behavior**
Data sent to i2s_write() should show up correctly on I2S bus.

**Impact**
Breaks I2S on RT595EVK.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- Zephyr SDK for RT595EVK, v3.4 of Zephyr @ commit 356c8cbe63ae01b3ab438382639d25bb418a0213 (v3.4.0 release)
comments:
The fix involves changes to both the dma driver and the i2s driver.

On the DMA driver side, it should assert that the source and dest data_sizes are the same, since the controller doesn't support different transfer sizes for src and dest. If the user were to specify different sizes, it's unclear which the driver should choose, and it might not match the user expectation/intent.

Also, since the documentation for the DMA controller in the RT595 states that memory addresses need to be aligned to the size, I think this should be asserted for as well, (e.g. a memory to peripheral transfer of 4 byte a a time would violate the alignment requirement if the memory address wasn't 4 byte aligned).

The I2S driver needs to change because it is currently setting source data size always to 1, instead of making it match the dest data_size. There are also other bugs in the I2S driver, like it not honoring the size passed to i2s_write(). I'll post a separate bug for this.

review_comments: This assert may cause failures in some of the other drivers that use this driver. I would suggest removing it and updating the comment.

If the caller has the dest_data_size == source_data_size, then the assert won't trip, and it won't trip if asserts are not enabled.

If the caller has different values for src and dest sizes, then it's a problem they need to think about and fix.
The old driver (prior to the change to support chaining for long transfers) used MIN. The driver
that supports the long transfers used MAX. This changing of behavior already broke existing drivers silently (e.g. the I2S usage). I think it'd be better to detect such problems as soon as possible, instead of silently doing something they might not be expecting and possibly setting the size the opposite of what the caller intended.
I know we will have to update the SPI driver to address this. Let me know if you would like me to send you a patch.

I can add that. I thought I had checked the SPI driver, since we use that too, but I think we didn't catch it because our usage of SPI is always using 1-byte dest_data_size (src_data_size is fixed at 1).
I think also the UART driver will be fine because destination and source data sizes will both be 1 always

I am not aware of such a alignment requirement. Were you seeing an issue?
There is a requirement for the DMA descriptors which this driver addresses.

In the RT500 Reference Manual, section 16.4.2.4 says:

> 16.4.2.4 Address alignment for data transfers
> Transfers of 16 bit width require an address alignment to a multiple of 2 bytes. Transfers of 32 bit width require an address alignment to a multiple of 4 bytes. Transfers of 8 bit width can be at any address

Ideally you should add only one patch per issue addressed. This way the code would be much easier to understand and review.

There are exceptions if the changes are tightly related. Not sure if this the case.

The primary bug is the change/regression in the DMA driver. But the fix to the DMA driver includes an assert, which is there to prevent future mistakes from happening silently. That assert would immediately break the I2S driver, which is why the two commits are combined in this PR.

I could take out the I2S one, but it would have to be merged first. I'm still relatively new to Zephyr (and github) development so I don't know if pull requests can be dependent on one another. Let me know if there's still a preference in having the I2S change be a separate Pull Request.
